note: From the 2026-08-05 MASAF register pass on comune Firenze (29 register entries). This was a deepening pass on an already-published city, not a new city. Leads failed only our evidence bar or the count; blocked can never ship as they stand. The 'off_cluster_currently_published' section is not a lead list, it is an observation about the live page for whoever next edits it. VERIFICATION PASS 2026-09-11: a brief asked this pass to re-verify seven old candidates from this file as if unpublished. Four (Monterey Cypress of Giardino Simone Weil, Strawberry Tree of Giardino dell'Iris, Chilean Wine Palm of Villa di Rusciano, Cypress of Villa della Petraia) turned out to already be live as flo_017, flo_020, flo_021 and flo_022, same names and coordinates, so this file was stale and never updated when those four shipped. Marked resolved below rather than deleted, so the mistake is visible. Do not re-dispatch them. VERIFICATION PASS 2026-09-12: worked the two remaining genuinely-Florence MASAF candidates from the passcheck brief's distance-ranked list (a Glicine at Via Pisana 130-132 turned out to be the SAME tree, same coordinates, as the already-blocked 'Wisteria of Via Pisana 130-132' above, nothing new there). The other two, MASAF 52 (Farnia, Mantignano) and MASAF 58 (Pioppo nero, Isolotto), verified clean against a second independent source (RAMI's own citizen-register pages) and were delivered to data/research/florence-verified.json as flo_025 and flo_026; both flagged for source disagreements on girth/height/age, both alive as of 2025/2026 updates, both confirmed-precision. Five more MASAF entries near Florence turned out to belong to neighbouring comuni (Bagno a Ripoli, Reggello) and are recorded below as wrong_city so nobody re-checks them. Also re-touched two open leads without resolving them: the Three Hackberries / Piazza Vasari alive-now question (evidence now leans toward felled, not spared) and the Black Pine of Villa Gamberaia access question (a promising but unverified 'pino laricio on the visit route' angle). Noticed but did not chase (would have been a fifth named candidate): RAMI's own Firenze listing carries a second poplar entry, 'Il Pioppo dell'Isolotto', distinct in name from the 'Il Pioppo dei Renaioli' delivered as flo_026; a future pass should check whether this is a register twin (same physical tree, two RAMI listings) before treating it as a fresh candidate.

leads.name: The Three Hackberries of the Cascine
leads.why: MASAF 54, 55 and 56/D612/FI/09, girths 407, 397 and 355 cm. REGISTER TRAP, recorded so the next pass does not repeat the work: these are three separate register entries for what a visitor sees as one group, exactly the double-counting pattern Setubal produced. If they ship they ship as ONE entry describing the group, with the other two sheet ids folded in as leads. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-11: the name is misleading and should change if this ever ships. It is NOT in the Cascine park (which sits ~4-5 km west along the Arno, see flo_005 at 11.228). RAMI's own per-tree page (ilregistrodeglialberi.it/16900) confirms AMI 56 at these exact coordinates as 'Bagolaro Piazza Vasari', girth 4.07 m matching MASAF's 397 or so, health 'Buona' as of an Oct 2025 measurement: this is Piazza Giorgio Vasari / the Campo di Marte green strip near Ponte al Pino, well inside the city, not the Cascine. A La Nazione piece dated 22 Nov 2025 (lanazione.it/firenze/cronaca/ponte-al-pino-alberi-wclqpl4h) reports RFI felling 21 trees in exactly this strip (15 bagolari among them) for temporary works during a railway bridge replacement, and says 'two of the four trees in the Piazza Vasari garden' carry the regional monumental designation, without stating whether those two survived the felling. That is a live 'alive now' question this pass could not close in two attempts: the register's own most recent measurement (Oct 2025) predates the felling announcement (Nov 2025) by weeks. NEXT PASS: check for a follow-up local news piece or a fresh street-level photo/satellite pass dated after Nov 2025 before shipping anything at this address, and rename it off 'Cascine' if it proceeds. RE-CHECKED AGAIN 2026-09-12, evidence now tips toward FELLED rather than spared: a WebSearch AI summary claimed 'the pine and historic trees present in the area will not be affected', but per the search-summary-is-a-lead-not-a-source rule this was NOT confirmed against a primary page (firenzetoday.it 403'd both attempts, comune.firenze.it's own Ponte al Pino notice page makes no mention of trees at all) and should be treated as unverified. Against it: lafirenzechevorrei.it's own headline reads 'Ponte al Pino, addio a 21 alberi storici: due sono nella lista regionale degli esemplari monumentali' (farewell to 21 historic trees: two are on the regional monumental list), 'addio' (farewell/goodbye) reading as past/decided rather than spared, and a Facebook post surfaced in search referencing '24 alberature storiche abbattute a Piazza [Vasari, unconfirmed]' in the past tense (felled), though a Facebook post is not independently verifiable and was not opened. RAMI's own page (16900) is still the pre-felling record, last touched 14 Oct 2025, health 'Buona', and shows no update since. STILL UNRESOLVED, still not shipped, but the next pass should treat 'probably felled' as the working assumption rather than 'probably fine', and look specifically for a 2026-dated photo, satellite pass, or a RAMI/comune update confirming either outcome before ever publishing this address.

leads.name: The Black Pine of Villa Gamberaia
leads.why: MASAF 09/D612/FI/09, girth 364 cm. RE-CHECKED 2026-09-11, access still unresolved rather than cleared. The comune's own 2026 press release (comune.firenze.it, 'Alberi monumentali, sono 29 le piante sotto tutela') and intoscana.it both independently name 'il famoso pino nero di Villa Gamberaia' as one of the 29 regionally listed trees and confirm it is among the 14 privately owned ones, which is a genuine second source for existence and species (MASAF plus these two republications). Villa Gamberaia's garden itself is a real ticketed public site (villagamberaia.com/en, Grandi Giardini Italiani: Mon-Sat 9:00-19:00 in season, EUR 20), so paid entry alone would not block it. What still blocks it: the villa's own visitor-facing garden page lists its planted species (cypress, box, yew, oak, lemon, olive) and does not mention a pine at all, and 'the Villa is not open to public visits, only the outdoor gardens are' -- so it is not established whether the registered pine stands inside the ticketed garden circuit or elsewhere on the private estate nearer the villa building. Two search attempts made, neither settled it. NEXT PASS: an OSM/aerial check for a large conifer crown within the mapped ticketed-garden boundary, or a source (photo, garden map, tour description) that places the pine explicitly on the visited route, would clear this either way. NEW ANGLE FOUND 2026-09-12, still not confirmed: a WebSearch summary of turismo.it's own garden writeup describes the visit route passing through the 'selvatico' (wild garden) toward the water parterre, and says visitors 'stop beneath the majestic Pino laricio (Corsican Pine) to appreciate the view of the Arno valley'. Pino laricio (Pinus nigra var. maritima / subsp. laricio) is a variety WITHIN Pinus nigra, the same species as the registered tree, so this could plausibly be the same pine and would settle the access question outright if confirmed on the visited circuit. NOT YET VERIFIED: two attempts to fetch the primary source directly failed (turismo.it/natura/articolo/art/villa-gamberaia-i-giardini-che-guardano-firenze-id-17633 returned HTTP 403; guidaperfirenze.com's fetched page turned out not to cover Villa Gamberaia at all), so per the search-summary-is-a-lead rule this quote has NOT been seen on the source itself and must not be treated as fact yet. NEXT PASS: fetch turismo.it via a different method (it 403s WebFetch; a browser-rendered fetch or cached copy may work), or find the same 'pino laricio in the selvatico, on the way to the water parterre' claim independently corroborated elsewhere, before shipping this tree as accessible.

leads.name: Further Orto Botanico trees on RAMI but not on MASAF
leads.species: Acer x peronai, Ginkgo biloba, Liriodendron tulipifera
leads.why: CHECKED 2026-08-22, still a lead, evidence bar not cleared. RAMI's own per-tree pages for all three (6486, 6489, 6493, registered 14 Oct 2021, updated 29 Dec 2024) carry ZERO measurements: no girth, no height, no age, and for ginkgo/tulip tree no coordinates either (only the maple has a GPS fix, 43.778719/11.262035, about 130 m from the flo_012 zelkova). English Wikipedia's Orto_Botanico_di_Firenze article independently confirms ginkgo and tulip tree are among the garden's species, which is a second source for existence/species only, not for remarkability: it lists them among dozens of species with no dates or measurements, unlike its treatment of the yew (1720) and cork oak (1805). More telling: the garden's OWN monumental-trees page (sma.unifi.it/vp-363), the same page that supplied the second source for flo_011-014, does NOT include ginkgo, tulip tree or the hybrid maple among its 8 named monumental specimens (it lists a newly-added Cupressus dupreziana instead). That is the institution itself drawing a line and leaving these three on the outside. The hybrid maple has one genuinely promising angle unexplored: Acer x peronai is described in Kew POWO and CABI-adjacent sources as one of the rarest European maples, with only about nine naturally-occurring wild individuals known, all in the Florence area, which would make a cultivated specimen in the collection historically/botanically significant regardless of size. No source found yet that documents this specific specimen's relationship to that wild population (age, provenance, whether it's a preserved wild individual or propagated). A search for the university's own dendrological collection inventory (a 'censimento globale delle collezioni' was reported launched August 2022, not yet public) or a scientific paper naming this specimen would settle it. Ginkgo and tulip tree remain thin leads with no remarkability evidence beyond bare presence; do not re-run the same RAMI/Wikipedia searches on a future pass without a new angle.

leads.name: Four Wikidata CC0 candidates (Q55742928, Q55742929, Q55742930, Q55742932) tagged as Florence
leads.species: Celtis australis, Quercus cerris, Cupressus sempervirens, Quercus pubescens
leads.why: CHECKED 2026-09-11: these are NOT Florence trees. All four carry catalog codes of the form NN/D575/FI/09, and D575 is the codice catastale for the comune of FIESOLE, not Firenze (Firenze itself is D612/FI/09, the code every other entry in this file uses). Their addresses (Terenzano-Compiobbi, Pian del Mugnone, Via del Bargellino, Torre a Buiano) are all in or near Fiesole, a separate hill town a few km northeast of Florence, reachable by ATAF bus in well under 30 minutes and a plausible day-trip candidate in its own right, but not currently a published city (no data/cities/fiesole.json exists) and out of scope for a Florence deepen pass. Q55742928 (the bagolaro with an image) is independently confirmed as Fiesole's own 'Bagolaro di Terenzano' via a RAMI page (ilregistrodeglialberi.it/14381). Do not fold these into Florence's candidate list again; if pursued, they belong to a Fiesole city brief (own verification pass, own four-candidate budget) or, if genuinely walkable from central Florence, an explicit day-trip entry with Fiesole named honestly as the place, per BRIEF_RESEARCH's day-trip rule.

leads.name: Five more MASAF entries near Florence that are not Florence trees (checked 2026-09-12)
leads.species: Cupressus sempervirens L. (x2), Quercus ilex L., Sequoiadendron giganteum, Chamaecyparis lawsoniana, Sequoia sempervirens
leads.why: CHECKED 2026-09-12, during a Florence deepen pass, by reading the 'comune' field directly off data/registers/italy-masaf.json rather than trusting distance-from-Florence-centre alone (the passcheck brief lists these by raw km distance, which does not know comune boundaries). None belong to Florence: a Cipresso comune at 43.753633/11.332725 (girth 510 cm) and a Leccio at 43.728556/11.31225 (girth 745 cm) both carry comune 'Bagno a Ripoli', a separate municipality southeast of Florence. Three more, a Sequoia gigante (girth 610 cm), a Cipresso di Lawson (girth 230 cm) and a Sequoia sempreverde (girth 840 cm), all three at Castello di Sammezzano near Leccio, comune 'Reggello', about 19 km away and belonging to a well-known separate tourist site (the castle and its park) rather than to Florence at all; also outside any reasonable day-trip transport boundary for a Florence page. Do not re-surface any of these five against Florence again; they would need their own city or day-trip brief for Bagno a Ripoli / Reggello / Sammezzano respectively, none of which are currently in scope.

blocked.name: The Stone Pine of the Cascine Pratone
blocked.reason: Dead. Felled by the windstorm of March 2015 according to the Tuscany monumental tree survey. Hidde's rule: no dead trees as entries, however large. Girth was about 4.5 m.

blocked.name: The Wisteria of Via Pisana 130-132
blocked.reason: Private property. The comune's own list records the ownership as private and the address is a residential street number, so hard rule 10 applies: not open to visitors, do not publish.

blocked.name: The Robinia of Via dei Pepi 7
blocked.reason: Private property. Recorded as privately owned in the comune's list, at a street number in the centre, with no evidence of public access. Attractive location for a walk and still blocked.

blocked.name: The Myrtle of Villa La Stella
blocked.reason: Private grounds, and not a collectible point. The Tuscany survey describes multiple stems of up to 50 cm circumference in the gardens of Villa La Stella, with a Dante-era age it marks as unconfirmed. A multi-stemmed shrub on private ground fails both the access rule and the one-identifiable-tree rule.

blocked.name: The Plane Trees of the Cascine avenue
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Described in the Tuscany survey as the planes along the avenue towards the former racecourse, with girths to about 6 m. An avenue has no single place to stand and nothing to have seen, the same test that removed Barcelona's La Rambla planes.

blocked.name: The trees of Villa Torrigiani
blocked.reason: Access-restricted private garden. The Tuscany survey lists a fine ginkgo of about 6 m girth, decapitated by a German grenade in September 1944 and recovered, but states that visits require a reservation made by telephone through a private contact. That is not publicly accessible in the sense this site promises, so it does not ship. Worth revisiting only if the garden publishes open visiting hours.

blocked.name: The Monterey Cypress of Largo Enrico Fermi
blocked.reason: CHECKED 2026-08-22. MASAF sheet 16/D612/FI/09, girth 480 cm, height 16.5 m, locality 'Larco Enrico Fermi, 5'. That address is the INAF Osservatorio Astrofisico di Arcetri (Arcetri Astrophysical Observatory), confirmed via the observatory's own site: the grounds are not open to casual visitors, only to booked guided tours ('Per Prenotazioni vai alla pagina delle Visite Guidate'; entrance for guided visits is at Via del Pian dei Giullari 16). Fails the 'can they get in without asking anyone's permission' test. Not private land in the residential sense, but access needs an advance reservation through the institute, so it stays blocked rather than shipped as an open access tree. Worth revisiting only if the observatory ever states the grounds (as opposed to the telescopes) are openly walkable, or if the tree is visible from a public road/path outside the perimeter (not checked this pass).
